baseline_models.mechanism: The imperative قُلْ and the discourse formula أَرَءَيْتُمْ open a commissioned thought experiment. The formula branch B013 is more precise here than literal eyesight alone.

changed_reading.before: A speaker asks the audience merely to look at a hypothetical event.
changed_reading.after: The messenger is commanded to make the audience evaluate and answer a pointed counterfactual.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: إِنْ أَهْلَكَنِىَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَن مَّعِىَ أَوْ رَحِمَنَا
baseline_models.mechanism: The conditional alternatives coordinate perishing and mercy under the same divine agency. The contrast concerns the speaker and those with him, but neither outcome alters the following question about the disbelievers.

activation_trace.role: supplies the causative prospect of perishing

changed_reading.before: The verse lists the speaker's death and survival as unrelated possibilities.
changed_reading.after: It balances divinely caused perishing against divine mercy while making both outcomes irrelevant to the disbelievers' liability.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: فَمَن يُجِيرُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
baseline_models.mechanism: The interrogative فَمَن and the separation phrase مِنْ عَذَابٍ make the protective-asylum branch of ج و ر decisive. The question presupposes that no protector can interpose between those who conceal the truth and painful punishment.

activation_trace.role: denotes granting asylum, protection, and prevention of harm

intensifies the punishment as actively pain-causing

changed_reading.before: The clause asks whether someone might generally help the disbelievers.
changed_reading.after: It issues an unanswerable challenge: no one can grant the disbelievers asylum from divinely imposed, pain-causing punishment.

discarded_or_unchanged: قُلْ remains ق و ل B001; the ق ل ل echo does not alter its morphology or translation.
يُجِيرُ remains ج و ر B003, protective asylum; ء ج ر B001 is not a competing derivation.
أَهْلَكَنِىَ selects perishing in ه ل ك B001, not the arid-land, wandering, or appetite branches.
عَذَابٍ selects punitive pain in ع ذ ب B005, not sweetness, abstention, or a dangling extremity.
أَلِيمٍ remains the pain-causing description in ء ل م B002.

strongest_changes: The repeated closing قُلْ chain turns the first-person conditional into a commissioned rebuttal rather than a private plea.
The 67:25-27 sequence makes the messenger's possible destruction or mercy irrelevant to the challengers' promised reckoning.
The close parallel with 67:20 makes يُجِيرُ an exclusive question of asylum: no army or other power can protect apart from the Merciful.
The ك ف ر plus ع ذ ب pairing and the immediate 67:27 antecedent identify a concrete, already threatened addressee group.
summary.what_was_special: Ayah 67:28 redirects hostile attention from the messenger's fate to the disbelievers' own exposure. Its force comes from a tightly staged closing sequence: demand for timing, divine ownership of knowledge, sight of the threat drawing near, an irrelevant counterfactual about the messenger, reliance on the Merciful, and a second أَرَءَيْتُمْ challenge.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not specify whether أَهْلَكَنِىَ evokes ordinary death, hostile hopes for the messenger's death, or both.
The scope of وَمَن مَّعِىَ is carried by unrooted function words and pronouns, so its exact social extent cannot be branch-traced here.
The nearby literal sight language strengthens the pressure of أَرَءَيْتُمْ, but the focus itself is still best assigned to formula branch B013 rather than literal-sight branch B001.
